title: Perceived latency vs hallucination: observability notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working note for designing a small set of SLIs and dashboard panels that intentionally connect user-perceived latency signals with basic hallucination/quality telemetry for text generation endpoints. Aim: give product and SRE teams a compact set of observability signals that explain when slow responses correlate with worse output quality, and surface cheap heuristics we can run in realtime as a first-line quality SLI.

Why this matters (short):
- Customers care about what the user sees: a 300ms server delta can feel different depending on when the first token arrives.
- Quality regressions (hallucinations) are often subtle and tied to fallback paths (e.g., model compression, quantized variants, partial prompt truncation) which can be triggered by routing/latency policies.
- Tying latency slices to quality heuristics helps prioritize incidents (e.g., high-latency + higher hallucination-rate = urgent).

High-level approach:
1) Define user-perceived latency SLI (single numeric value): typical aggregation = p95 of "time-to-first-stream-token" from client SDK + fraction of requests where TTFST > 500ms.
2) Define lightweight hallucination SLI (probabilistic): sketch a "cheap signal" that runs on first N tokens + available metadata and flags likely hallucinations. No oracle required — heuristics only.
3) Produce dashboard that cross-plots latency buckets vs hallucination-rate by model, route, and customer tier.

Proposed signals and definitions (working):
- client_ttfst_ms (client-observed): time from request start to first token delivered to client. Source: client SDK metric (fallback: edge proxy first byte).
- server_compute_ms: time spent in inference runtime (span: inference.compute).
- queue_wait_ms: time in scheduler queue before being scheduled.
- total_server_latency_ms: queue_wait_ms + server_compute_ms + serialization_ms.
- net_rtt_ms: approximated as client_ttfst_ms - total_server_latency_ms (negative values => clock skew; cap at 0).

User-perceived SLI (primary):
- name: user_ttfst_p95_ms
- definition: p95(client_ttfst_ms) over 5m windows, per-route and per-model.
- alert trigger (proposal): p95 > 800ms for 10m sustained, or p95 increase > 2x baseline and absolute > 500ms.

User-experience SLI (secondary):
- name: streaming-start-fraction
- definition: fraction of streaming requests that deliver first token within 300ms.
- intent: capture impact of batching/continuous-prefetch on perceived responsiveness.

Cheap hallucination heuristic (quality SLI):
- name: heuristic-hallucination-flag (binary per-response)
- inputs we can compute in realtime: o language-model entropy proxies (e.g., avg token surprise using top-k token probs if available), o hallucination keywords match (domain-specific lists), o url-claimed-entity mismatch (if external fact-checks are cheap), o improbable named-entity co-occurrence (basic heuristic), o short-answer contradiction heuristic (if response includes disclaimers like "I might be wrong" flagged).
- scoring: each heuristic = 1 point; flag if points >= 2 for initial rollout.
- aggregation: hallucination_rate = rate(flagged) per 5m by model, route, customer-tier.

Notes on feasibility:
- Some models don't return token-level probabilities in hosted flow. Fallback: compute ngram-surprise using a tiny local LM or use client-side signal (user edits, subsequent clarifying prompts) as delayed quality signal.
- Keyword lists should be curated per vertical to avoid noise. Start with a small public list (dates, statute names, firm names) and iterate.

Tracing/span design suggestions (trace annotations to capture both latency and hints about quality):
- trace root: request.receive -> user metadata (route, model_id, customer_tier)
- span inference.scheduling: tags: queue_len, host_shard_id, priority_policy
- span inference.compute: tags: gpu_type, sequence_length, kv_cache_hit_ratio, quantization_profile, fallback_model (if any), batch_size
- span inference.postprocess: tags: truncate_applied (bool), safety_triggers (list), hallucination_heuristic_score (int) — add as tag to make correlation easier in searches
- client-observed span: client.wait_for_first_token_ms (captured by SDK and attached when available)

Dashboard panel ideas (compact page):
1) Top row: small KPI tiles: user_ttfst_p95_ms, streaming-start-fraction, hallucination_rate (global).
2) Heatmap: model vs route, cell shows p95 TTFST with overlaid sparklines for hallucination_rate. Color rule: high latency + hallucination_rate above baseline -> bright red.
3) Scatter: each request sample (sampled) plotted by client_ttfst_ms (x) vs hallucination_heuristic_score (y). Add density contours and a regression line.
4) Time-series: stacked view of p50/p95 client_ttfst_ms with annotated deploys/fallback-events. Include a secondary axis with hallucination_rate.
5) Trace-linked table: recent traces where hallucination_flagged=true sorted by client_ttfst_ms desc. Click to open full trace.

PromQL / query sketches (pseudo):
- p95_ttfst: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(client_ttfst_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model))
- hallucination_rate: sum(rate(hallucination_flag_count[5m])) by (route, model) / sum(rate(request_count[5m])) by (route, model)
- correlation panel: sum(rate(hallucination_flag_count[5m])) by(route) / sum(rate(request_count[5m])) by(route) vs histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(client_ttfst_ms_bucket[5m])) by(route)

Alerting guidance (starter):
- Priority P0 (oncall interrupt): hallucination_rate > 2% AND user_ttfst_p95_ms > 1000ms sustained for 10m for top-5 revenue routes.
- Priority P1 (paged but lower urgency): model-level hallucination_rate increase > 300% relative to trailing 7d baseline and absolute > 0.5% for 30m.
- Diagnostic alert (noting): queue_wait_ms p95 > 200ms triggers runbook to look at scheduler capacity.

Data quality and sampling notes:
- Do not compute hallucination heuristics on 100% of global traffic initially (compute cost). Start with 5–10% sampling grouped by customer_tier. When a model or route looks suspicious, switch to 100% for that model/route for 1h.
- Persist flagged responses to a short-term indices (30d) for retrospective labeling and model/eval feedback. Include original prompt + response + heuristic flags + trace id.

Quick runbook snippets (for incidents):
- If user_ttfst_p95 rises sharply with stable server_compute_ms but increased net_rtt_ms => investigate edge/CDN, TLS renegotiation, cloud region networking.
- If hallucination_rate rises and fallback_model tag present on traces => examine routing config and rollback fallback or increase weight of verified variant.
- If hallucination_rate rises and avg token_surprise high => likely model-quality regression; escalate to model-onboarding/research.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which heuristics give acceptable precision/recall? Need labeled dataset (bootstrap via human review).
- Where to run heuristics: sidecar in runtime vs separate telemetry worker? Sidecar cheaper for context, worker cheaper for compute isolation.
- Wire client SDK TTFST into traces without violating PII/data residency for private deployments.

Next steps (practical roadmap):
- 2-week spike: implement 5% realtime heuristic computation in telemetry worker for two routes (chat and completion-default).
- Build dashboard M0 with KPI tiles + one heatmap. Iterate with product team.
- Create labeling queue (manual review UI) for flagged responses and collect 500 labeled items for precision estimate.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on heuristics to avoid noisy paging. The goal is actionable signal, not perfect detection.
- Feedback: prefer concrete prioritized heuristics to try first (Marco suggested entity mismatch and disclaimer text).

Action items (owners):
- Marco: prototype hallucination heuristic worker and add metric hallucination_flag_count. (Due: 2024-11-08)
- Lina: add client TTFST SDK hook and short doc for data privacy constraints. (Due: 2024-11-15)
- Owen: dashboard shell in Grafana and basic queries. (Due: 2024-11-22)

End of note.
